interpretation: Return-year Braun-Blanquet state is directionally lower in points that are lost again, but it does not add robust fragility information after pre-loss local history, loss-year vegetation continuity, source point abundance, stable node identity, and return year are represented. Recovery debt and return fragility are therefore parallel features of incomplete recovery rather than a demonstrated abundance-mediated pathway.
ecological_update: Observed recovery has at least two partially distinct dimensions: returned points are quantitatively depressed on average, and returned points are more likely to be lost again; current data do not show that the abundance debt itself explains the elevated re-loss.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc fragility mechanism-discrimination on an already-opened exact-point recovery endpoint.
Do not claim that low return-year Braun-Blanquet mediates or causes subsequent re-loss; the frozen coefficient interval overlaps zero.
The negative point estimate and lower mean BB among re-lost returns are descriptive and do not replace the failed support rule.
Recorded re-loss is an observation-state transition, not mortality or demographic relapse.
Braun-Blanquet is ordinal abundance, not percent cover or biomass.
Do not retune recovery patterns, controls, history terms, quantitative inclusion, or model to rescue a return-quality mechanism.
